name: Kaempferia parviflora (black ginger)
short: Case report (title only): anaphylaxis to black ginger in a supplement. Trials (4 to 12 weeks, adults): no extract-related adverse events. Animal/lab data: lowered sildenafil, raised midazolam levels.
text: Allergy: a case report is titled 'Case of anaphylaxis caused by black ginger in a dietary supplement'; the record has no abstract, so the patient, the product, its other ingredients, how it was taken and the outcome cannot be reported, and the title does not give the plant's Latin name, so it is not confirmed that the black ginger was Kaempferia parviflora. In a 4-week randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled safety trial of a Kaempferia parviflora extract in 52 healthy Japanese adults, there were no adverse events related to the extract and no abnormalities compared with placebo in body measurements, heart and circulation measures, or blood and urine tests. In a 12-week placebo-controlled trial in 76 overweight and preobese Japanese adults, neither group had adverse events related to the test foods or clinically relevant abnormal changes in physical examination, blood or urine tests. A 2017 systematic review of 7 clinical studies found no adverse events reported, including at 1.35 g a day, but calls for further studies of safety. In a 30-day open-label study in 14 men aged 50 to 68 with mild erectile dysfunction (13 completed), the authors describe the rhizome extract as well tolerated, without listing events. These trials were short and in adults; the cited abstracts give no data for pregnancy, breastfeeding or long-term use. Interactions (animal and laboratory data only): in rats, the extract lowered blood levels of sildenafil (area under the curve 60 to 65% lower); in human liver microsomes it inhibited CYP3A, a major enzyme that breaks down many medicines, and in rats it raised blood levels of midazolam 2.3-fold, with the authors suggesting a food-drug interaction. These results point in opposite directions for the two medicines, and the cited abstracts report no human interaction study.
